Subject: Request: assessment of metering impact for JSON-mode + tool invocations

Hi Emma —

Thanks for the quick onboarding call yesterday. BuildWise is evaluating Redwood for several features that will rely heavily on structured outputs (JSON mode) and frequent tool/function invocations (webhook + product catalog lookups). Before we schedule pricing review with procurement, can you send a short baseline on how these two usage patterns are metered on the hosted API? Specifically we need:

- Per-unit baseline rates (hosted API): tokens (input vs output), per-1k-token numbers for generation and for embedding where applicable.
- How JSON-mode (structured output enforcement) affects metering — is there any additional per-request charge for validation/schema enforcement, or is it purely token-based?
- Per-invocation cost for tool/function calls (if any) — do you charge a flat invocation fee in addition to token charges? How are request/response payloads counted?
- Discount/packaging guidance: what thresholds (monthly committed spend) unlock X% off? Any swap to include tool-call allowances vs per-call billing?

I attached a small sample of our observed workload (usage_sample.csv) and a rough forecast. If you can get a conservative rate card back that calls out the points above, procurement will want a formal quote. We’d like to decide whether to ask for a pilot-friendly waived tool-call fee vs a commit-driven discount.

Target timeline: received by EOD Tuesday (7/20) would be ideal so procurement can review before next week’s renewal sync.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Hi Karthik —

Thanks for the clear ask and for the sample. I pulled the initial rate guidance together and attached an annotated ratecard PDF (buildwise_requested_ratecard_v1.pdf). High-level notes here so procurement has something to work from: 

1) Token charging (hosted API):
   - Standard generation: billed per 1K tokens (input + output). Example baseline: $0.030 / 1K tokens for generation model families (this is illustrative and region-dependent).
   - Embeddings: billed separately per 1K embedding units (example $0.012 / 1K).

2) JSON-mode / structured output: 
   - The model output is charged as normal token usage (output token count). There is no separate per-request token surcharge for JSON-mode purely for serialization.
   - If you enable Redwood’s server-side schema validation or structured post-processing (automatic retries, schema repair), those validation steps are implemented as internal function calls and are metered as "tool invocations" (see below) unless you select the "validation not-metered" enterprise option.

3) Tool / function invocation metering: 
   - Tool calls (external HTTP webhooks, K/V lookups, and Redwood-managed function hooks) are billed as: flat per-invocation fee + standard token charges for any model input/output generated as part of that invocation. Current baseline example: $0.0025 per tool call + token usage.
   - Payloads (tool request/response bodies) are counted towards token totals when they pass through the model (i.e., if you include tool output in the model prompt or response). Purely opaque tool calls that do not interact with the model are not token-billed but still incur the per-invocation fee.

4) Discount / packaging: 
   - Usage tiers (illustrative): 10% off at $50k/mo committed; 20% off at $200k/mo; 30%+ negotiable for multi-region enterprise with 12+ month commit and usage guarantees.
   - We can structure a package that includes a tool-call allowance (e.g., 10M calls/mo) bundled into a committed plan to avoid per-invocation fees after the allowance is consumed (preferred for high-call-rate patterns).

Next steps: I can get legal/finance a draft quote if BuildWise confirms an expected monthly token volume and an approximate tool-call count (monthly). If helpful, we can also scope an enterprise option where internal validation calls are excluded from metering.

I attached the PDF and a link to our HubSpot deal for reference. Happy to jump on a 30-min call.

Best,
Emma Li
Head of Strategic Accounts, BuildWise

Thanks for forwarding — Emma, good write-up. A few negotiation suggestions from GTM/finance side before we commit to numbers: 

- Pilot incentive: offer waived per-invocation fee for the first 90 days (still bill tokens) to reduce initial friction. Then move to a committed plan if BuildWise hits agreed-upon throughput.
- Packaging: for customers where tool-call volume dwarfs token consumption, we typically offer a tier that bundles a large tool-call allowance and reduces the token rate slightly. Example proposal to present: 12mo commit at $60k/mo -> 18% discount + 8M included tool calls/mo; per-call fee after allowance $0.0015.
- Conditional clause: if actual token usage exceeds forecast by >30% for 2 consecutive months, we reserve the right to revisit pricing (protects against runaway token costs).

Diego/Neha — can you confirm if we can (a) enable a flag to mark validation calls as non-metered on an enterprise tenant, or (b) offer a config where schema validation runs as a non-metered pre-check (technical workaround)? If neither is feasible, we should clearly call out the added cost to the customer.

Marissa

Quick technical take — copying Emma so she has the notes: 

- JSON-mode output itself is just token-billed. However, our schema validator runs as a server-side pass that can optionally call the model to repair/normalize outputs ("auto-repair"). Those repair calls generate model tokens and, in current hosted plans, are counted as tool-invocations + token usage.
- Options to reduce billed invocations: 
  1) Batch validation: group multiple small validation requests into a single model call for repair where latency allows; this lowers per-invocation counts but adds complexity to client workflow.
  2) Offer an enterprise config flag that marks validation as "control-plane" activity and excludes it from customer metering (requires product + billing opt-in; acceptable for committed enterprise deals).
  3) Client-side lightweight validation library we can publish (open-source) to drop the need for server-side repairs in many cases.

Given BuildWise’s 5–12M call estimate, recommending option #2 bundled with the committed plan (structure Marissa suggested). I attached a sketch of possible packaging economics (pricing_model_sketch.png).

- Diego
